Paul King

This article is about the man himself. For the free online encyclopedia he does not personally endorse, see Wikipedia (disambiguation). Not to be confused with Paul King (film director), who has never once been asked to double-check a fact at a dinner party.

Paul King is a British-American systems administrator, former executive chef, and unofficial human search engine based in Louisville, Kentucky. Naturalized as a United States citizen in October 2025 following nine years of residency, King has developed a reputation among friends and colleagues for an unusually complete and rapidly-retrievable base of general knowledge — a trait several acquaintances have described, without apparent irony, as "faster than looking it up."[citation needed]

Early life and education

King trained in the United Kingdom, earning Higher National Diplomas in Computer Software Engineering (Lakes College, 2000–2002) and Management Information Systems (University of Worcester, 2002–2004) — an unusual academic foundation for a man who would go on to spend the next decade in professional kitchens before returning to technology.

Career

Culinary career. Before his transition into enterprise IT, King held a distinguished career as a professional chef. Colleagues have noted this period "afforded him thick skin, conflict resolution, and delegation and leadership skills" — a description King himself has never disputed, possibly because it is taken directly from his own professional biography. Despite leaving professional kitchens, King is reported to still instinctively organize any gathering according to mise en place. Former colleagues note that his transition to systems administration produced a measurable decrease in shouting, but no decrease in precision.

Technology career. From 2011 to 2019, King worked as a self-employed consultant technician in the United Kingdom. He briefly served as an MSAS Agent supporting USAA (2019–2020) before joining Gordon-Darby, Inc. in February 2020, where he currently serves as System Administrator II. King has publicly characterized his role as occupying "the grey area between DevOps and IAM" — a phrase now considered, within his circle, to be his personal motto.

Naturalization

In October 2025, King became a naturalized citizen of the United States after nine years of residency. The occasion is noted here not because it relates to his information-recall abilities, but because it is objectively a big deal and this article's editors insisted.

Announcing the occasion himself, King wrote: "Took a day off yesterday to cement my commitment to the United States. The last 6 years has been a pleasure, now the rest of my life will be a treasure."[self-published source]

Independence Day (2026)

On July 4, 2026, King hosted his first Independence Day cookout as a naturalized citizen — an occasion held roughly eight months after his naturalization, and one attendees have already begun describing, without obvious hyperbole, as one of the most significant events of his life. Fireworks were procured. A grill was involved. Local sources have already begun describing it as the most extra cookout in postal code history.

Drawing on the professional culinary background documented elsewhere in this article, King is reported to have approached the cookout with a level of technical precision rarely observed outside of laboratory conditions, resulting in what one attendee called "the most thoroughly optimized brisket of the twenty-first century." The fireworks display was, by all accounts, coordinated with a commitment to timing accuracy that several guests found "unnecessary but appreciated."

The occasion is considered historically significant by at least two people, and increasingly significant the longer the fireworks continue.

While King officially became an American citizen in October 2025, several editors consider this cookout to be the ceremonial completion of the process.

The Floki Farstrider persona

Under the alias Floki Farstrider, King is described in at least one personal profile as the "Avatar of the Horned God" and "mortal incarnation of Auriel." Scholars of the subject note that this is, functionally, a second Wikipedia infobox King wrote about himself without any input from the actual website — a detail frequently raised by his friends as evidence that he does not hate the concept of an encyclopedia, only the specific one that isn't about him.

Cannabis expertise

Outside of his professional work, King has developed an extensive interest in cannabis science, particularly terpene chemistry, cultivar selection, extraction methods, and cannabinoid interactions. Friends have described his approach as "less recreational and more peer-reviewed." Casual questions on the subject frequently develop into detailed discussions involving chemistry, cultivation history, and optimization strategy — consistent with his broader pattern of treating every field of interest as one requiring rigorous methodology.[citation needed]

Relationship with Dakota

King first met longtime friend Dakota while the two were living as neighbors in Louisville, Kentucky, more than six years prior to the events described elsewhere in this article. According to both parties, each had independently identified the other as a fellow enthusiast of recreational cannabis well before any formal introduction took place. King is credited with extending the invitation that led to their first shared session — an offer historians of the friendship consider less an icebreaker than a formality.

Years later, King met Susanna Conway during a visit centered on cannabis chemistry and terpene profiles. The conversation eventually turned to Wikipedia's open editing model, a topic which — through a sequence of events this article's editors consider self-evident — led directly to the creation of this article.

Public records of the friendship show an unbroken annual tradition of birthday well-wishes dating back to at least 2021, a level of consistency editors note is unusual for two men who otherwise communicate primarily through memes about pirates, mushrooms, and pugs with road rage.

The Wikipedia dispute

On the Fourth of July, during a conversation at a social gathering, the subject of Wikipedia's editability was raised. King, drawing on deeply held convictions regarding information integrity, categorized the platform as "fake news" — a position that proved unusually energizing for at least one other attendee. In response, it was proposed, apparently spontaneously, that the next time anyone checked Wikipedia, they would find something about him.

This article is the result.

"Who needs Wikipedia when you have Paul?" — attributed, disputed, currently under discussion on the Talk page.
Personal life

King shares his home with one Cavalier King Charles Spaniel, a breed historically favored by British nobility — a detail some editors have flagged as thematically consistent with his self-described divine status, and others have flagged as a coincidence.

Trivia
  • Is widely believed to know not just a little bit about a lot, but a lot about a lot.
  • Has never once said "let me Google that."
  • Is the only known subject of a Wikipedia article who would prefer it did not exist.
  • Semi-professionally disputes his own notability.
  • "It's always DNS." Editors remain divided on whether this statement is technically accurate or spiritually accurate.
  • Has been known to distinguish between "medium rare" and "medium legendary," a distinction editors have declined to define further.

Bibliography

King is the author of The Raven: A Trip to the English Lake District (2024), a novella following archaeologist Henry Contini and his wife Danielle as they travel to the Lake District and find themselves drawn into a considerably older mystery: the disappearance of a 250-strong Roman garrison at Hardknot Fort in 105 AD, and the shapeshifting demon responsible for it. Originally written in 1996, it is one of several short stories composed during the author's youth, published in its original form decades later.

Written1996
Published2024
GenreFolk horror; cryptozoology-adjacent

Plot. The demon, named Fangoria, can only be harmed by a pair of obsidian daggers roughly 7,000 years old. Danielle, 48, is mistaken for Henry's daughter by a taxi driver within the first chapter — a joke King revisits more than once. The novella repeats its own warning at both its opening and its close: "Beware the beast that rides the lightning."

The plot's central weapon requirement — daggers of considerable age and provenance — has been noted by some readers as thematically consistent with King's well-documented preference for verifiable primary sources.[citation needed]
